Paper / Title (Year): This comparative analysis situates the proposed RLFA-CNN within the broader landscape of waste classification research from 2021 to 2026.
While heavy transfer-learning models (e.g., EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV2, ECCDN-Net) achieve peak accuracies in the 92-96% range,
they demand millions of parameters and substantial computational overhead. In contrast, older or aggressively pruned models (e.g., SVM, IoT CNNs, VGG16)
struggle to break the 88% accuracy barrier.
The proposed RLFA-CNN strikes an optimal balance: by replacing the standard Flatten layer with Global Average Pooling (GAP) and applying L1 Regularization,
it achieves a highly competitive 90.50% accuracy using only ~111,000 parameters.
Most importantly, it maintains an exceptional 93.7% recall rate on recyclable materials, proving it is a highly viable, edge-ready architecture.
